title: Jolt RigidBody3D capsules "sink" into static bodies (landing from gravity reproduction example)
body:
### Tested versions

4.5.1 using Godot Jolt Physics (can also be reproduced with GodotPhysics3D)

### System information

Tested on Windows 10, Linux Mint 22.2 & Linux Fedora 43 (varied mid to high range hardware)

### Issue description

**Context:** In order to achieve fast falling for RigidBody based character controllers after jump or dropping off ledges (and pretty much get rid of perceived default 9.8 floatyness of rigidbodies in a global manner), a high gravity value is set globally in project physics configuration, for example, 100. 

While applying default gravity or much lower than the proposed 100 may be enough and even look good for many games, certain games require this type of descent speed which accentuates an undesired rigidbody capsule sinking effect that can usually also be perceived at the default 9.8 gravity.

It is possible other approaches could be taken to apply such descent speeds, such as manually adding forces, but this would complicate things, and setting a global gravity for all rigid bodies seems like the cleanest approach.

**Expected:** Capsules should just stay on the ground on land with no perceptible sink or penetration.

**What actually happens:** On land, capsules sink slightly and resurface, finally staying at ground level. The capsule seems to penetrate the StaticBody3D floor for around 7 frames. In the MRP I print logs which point to these frames it takes for the rigidbody to resurface, and you can also see how the capsule clips into the floor.

From the MRP:
https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/348ca001-651d-4933-92c0-b4ae0e11bf49

**Issue:** A very perceptible visual “sink” occurs for rigidbody3d character controllers for example. In my case (not the MRP, some other 3D games I’m making) my rigidbody capsule collision based characters very visually sink into the ground on land which looks bad visually, and since my main game (not MRP)'s camera system follows height coordinates, the effect is further accentuated by the camera movement. But I think capsule collision is still the best choice for dealing with ramps and other uneven surfaces.

**What I’ve tried:** I’ve been investigating workarounds for this issue for a few years now and I already tried quite a few physics configurations, most notably increasing physics ticks to 120 (which seems to help slightly, but doesn’t really get rid of the issue). This only happens with capsule collision afaik (considering their shape, it may also occur with spheres? but I haven’t tried this yet), switching to more flat bottom shapes offering more landing surface helps a lot, but sometimes just isn’t reasonable for character controllers.

**The following discussion topic was initiated before creating this issue, it includes alternate approaches, alternate MRP, and main project reproduction example, and workaround solutions attempted, as well as any further details I may have missed to include in this bug report:**
https://forum.godotengine.org/t/godot-jolt-rigidbody-capsule-ground-sink/129546

However none of the investigated workarounds _cleanly_ solve this issue (for reasons also discussed in topic).

**This issue was also discussed on the official Godot discord:** Where user named "_booch" Suggested using a CharacterController3D instead, and very interestingly, showcased the fact that this sinking behaviour doesn't happen with inbuilt character controllers (I haven't tested this myself yet though): 

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f8ca1163-cd73-4eef-b31b-0cbfd5e19069

However, my main objection to switching to CharacterController3D is that, afaik, applying additive forces to a CharacterController3D isn't as trivial (even though additive forces could likely be calculated by outputting to a final velocity, I'd rather let Godot Jolt do that cleaner internally), I'd rather use a rigidbody where in theory I should have more fine tuned / dynamic control. But I might still give it a try if there's just no other way. It still doesn't draw away from the fact that this rigidbody shape doesn't behave as expected with completely or very close to default physics values though.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Create a new 3D godot scene (I've also reproduced this in 2D).
2. Add a RigidBody3D, and a CollisionShape3D as child, then select a Capsule Collision for that collision shape.
3. Add Camera3D pointing to this setup.
4. Place the RigidBody3D 5+ meters above the ground.
5. Ensure / switch to Jolt Physics in Godot's 3D physics configuration.
6. Save and reload, then run the project and appreciate described symptoms.
7. If the sinking effect isn't appreciated, increase gravity. The sinking effect should be certainly visible at gravity 100.

or:

1. Inspect and run MRP provided.

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

https://github.com/Mangonels/capsule-gravity-ground-penetration
